translation_en: Hind bint Utbah came and said, O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a miserly man. Is there any blame on me if I feed our children from what belongs to him? He replied, No, except according to what is fair. Aishah reported Hind's question and the Prophet's reply about giving the family what was fair.

Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said, If a woman spends from her husband's earnings without his instruction, she receives half of his reward. Abu Huraira related this statement from the Prophet about a wife's spending from her husband's earnings.

Ali reported that Fatimah came to the Prophet complaining of pain in her hand from grinding. She had heard servants had been brought to him but did not find him, so she told Aishah. When he came, Aishah informed him. He came to us while we had gone to bed. We started to get up, but he said, Stay where you are. He sat between us until I felt the coolness of his feet on my stomach. He said, Shall I tell you something better than what you asked for? When you go to bed, glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Allah thirty-three times, and declare Allah's greatness thirty-four times. That is better for you than a servant.

Fatimah came to the Prophet asking him for a servant. He said, Shall I tell you something better for you? Glorify Allah thirty-three times when you go to sleep, praise Allah thirty-three times, and declare Allah's greatness thirty-four times. Sufyan added that one of these should be said thirty-four times. Ali said, I have not stopped doing this since. He was asked, Not even on the night of Siffin? He replied, Not even on the night of Siffin.

Al-Aswad bin Yazid asked Aishah what the Prophet used to do at home. She said, He would serve his family, and when he heard the call to prayer, he would go out. This is Aishah's description of his conduct with his household before he left for prayer.

Hind bint Utbah said, O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is stingy and does not give me enough for myself and my children unless I take from his property without his knowledge. Is there any blame on me? He said, Take what is enough for you and your children, according to what is fair.

Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah said, The best of the women who rode camels were the women of Quraysh. Another narrator said: The righteous women of Quraysh are the most compassionate toward a child in its youth and the most careful with a husband's property. This report was narrated by Abu Huraira from the Messenger of Allah.

Ali said that the Prophet gave him a striped garment. He wore it, but saw anger on the Prophet's face, so he tore it into pieces and distributed them among his womenfolk. Ali then divided the garment among his wives.

Jabir bin Abdullah said: My father died leaving seven or nine daughters, so I married a previously married woman. The Messenger of Allah asked if I had married. I said yes. He asked whether she was a virgin or previously married. I said previously married. He said, Why not a young virgin, so that you could play with her and she with you, and make one another laugh? I told him my father Abdullah had died leaving daughters. I did not want to bring them someone of their own age, so I married a woman who could look after them and set things right for them. He said, May Allah bless you, or he said something good.

A man came to the Prophet and said, I am ruined. He asked why. The man said he had intercourse with his wife during Ramadan. The Prophet said, Free a slave. The man replied that he could not. He said, Then fast for two consecutive months. The man replied that he could not. He said, Then feed sixty poor people. The man replied that he could not find the means. A basket of dates was brought, and the Prophet asked where the questioner was. The man said, Here I am. The Prophet told him, Give this in charity. The man said, To someone poorer than us, Messenger of Allah? By the One who sent you with the truth, there is no household between these two lava fields poorer than ours. The Prophet laughed until his teeth showed and said, Then it is for you.

Umm Salamah said, I asked the Messenger of Allah whether I would be rewarded for spending on the sons of Abu Salamah. I cannot leave them in this condition; they are my own sons. He said, Yes. You will have the reward for whatever you spend on them.
Hind asked the Messenger of Allah whether it was wrong to take from Abu Sufyan's property what was enough for her and her children, since he was stingy. He said, Take what is fair and sufficient.

Abu Huraira reported that a deceased man who owed a debt was brought to the Messenger of Allah. He asked if the man had left enough to repay it. If told the debt was covered, he prayed over him; otherwise he told the Muslims, Pray over your companion. Later, when Allah granted him conquests, he said, I am closer to the believers than they are to themselves. Whoever dies among the believers leaving a debt, I will repay it; whoever leaves property, it belongs to his heirs.

Umm Habibah asked the Prophet to marry her sister, the daughter of Abu Sufyan. He asked if she wanted that. She said yes, explaining she was not his only wife and would love her sister to share in the good. He said this was not lawful for him. She said people had told her he wanted to marry Durrah, daughter of Abu Salamah. He clarified that she meant Umm Salamah's daughter. He explained that even if she were not his stepdaughter in his care, she would still not be lawful for him. She was his niece through breastfeeding: Thuwaybah breastfed both him and Abu Salamah. He said not to offer their daughters or sisters to him. Urwah reported from al-Zuhri that Abu Lahab had freed Thuwaybah.

The Prophet said, Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and release the captive. Sufyan explained that the captive is a prisoner. This report was narrated by Abu Musa al-Ashari, and Sufyan explained the term used for the captive.
The family of Muhammad did not eat their fill of food for three days in succession before he passed away. This was reported by Abu Huraira about the Prophet's family.

Abu Huraira said hunger once overcame him. He asked Umar to recite a Quran verse with him; Umar went inside and opened the door for him. Abu Huraira walked a little way, then collapsed face down from hunger and weakness. The Messenger of Allah found him, took his hand, helped him up, understood his condition, and brought him to his lodging. He ordered a large bowl of milk. Abu Huraira drank, and the Prophet told him to drink again until he was full. Abu Huraira later told Umar what had happened and said, Allah entrusted this to someone more deserving than you. By Allah, I asked you to recite the verse though I know it better than you. Umar replied, By Allah, I would have been happier to bring you in than to own the finest red camels.

Umar bin Abi Salamah said, I was a boy in the care of the Messenger of Allah, and my hand moved around the dish. The Messenger of Allah said to me, Boy, mention Allah's name, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you. That remained my way of eating afterward.

Umar bin Abi Salamah said, One day I ate with the Messenger of Allah, reaching around the dish for food. He told me, Eat from what is nearest to you. This report was transmitted by Abd al-Aziz bin Abdullah from Muhammad bin Jafar, from Muhammad bin Amr bin Halhala al-Dili, from Wahb bin Kaysan, from Umar bin Abi Salamah, who was the son of Umm Salamah, the Prophet's wife. He related this instruction he received while eating with the Messenger.
Food was brought to the Messenger of Allah, with his stepson Umar bin Abi Salamah present. He told him, Mention Allah's name and eat from what is nearest to you.

A tailor invited the Messenger of Allah to a meal he had prepared. Anas went with him and saw him picking pieces of gourd from around the dish. Anas said, From that day on, I have always loved gourd. Anas said this happened at a meal prepared by the tailor.

Aishah said the Prophet liked to begin with the right whenever possible: in purification, putting on footwear, combing his hair, and in all his affairs. Masruq related this from Aishah, who described these actions as things the Prophet preferred.

Abu Talhah told Umm Sulaym, I heard the Messenger of Allah's voice sounding weak and recognized hunger in it. Do you have anything? She brought barley loaves, wrapped them in part of her head-covering, tucked them under Umar's garment, and sent him to the Messenger of Allah. He found him in the mosque with people and delivered the message. The Prophet asked whether Abu Talhah had sent him with food. Umar said yes. The Prophet told those with him, Get up. He and the people went to Abu Talhah's house. Abu Talhah said, Umm Sulaym, the Messenger of Allah has brought people, and we do not have enough food for them. She replied, Allah and His Messenger know best. Abu Talhah went out and met the Prophet, then they both came in. The Prophet asked Umm Sulaym to bring what she had. She brought the bread; he had it broken up, and she squeezed clarified butter from a small skin and used it as relish. After the Prophet said what Allah willed, he told them to let ten people enter. They ate until full and went out. He repeated this until all the people had eaten their fill. They were eighty men. This account was transmitted by Malik from Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, who heard Anas describe Abu Talhah and Umm Sulaym's hospitality.

Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr said: We were with the Prophet, one hundred and thirty people. He asked whether anyone had food. A man had about a measure of food, which was kneaded. Then a tall, shaggy-haired polytheist came driving sheep. The Prophet asked, Are you selling them, giving them, or offering them as a gift? The man said he was selling them. The Prophet bought a sheep. It was prepared, and he ordered its liver to be roasted. By Allah, each of the one hundred and thirty people received a piece of its liver; if present, it was given to him, and if absent, it was set aside for him. The food was placed in two large bowls. We all ate and were satisfied, and food remained. I loaded the remainder onto a camel.
Aishah said, The Prophet passed away after we had eaten our fill of the two dark foods: dates and water. This was reported by Aishah.

Suwayd bin al-Numan said: We went with the Messenger of Allah to Khaybar. When we reached al-Sahba, a place about an afternoon's journey from Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah called for food, but only roasted barley flour mixed with water was brought. We chewed and ate it. Then he called for water; he rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed ours. He led us in the sunset prayer without performing ablution again. Sufyan said, I heard this from him more than once, at the beginning and afterward.
Anas said, The Prophet did not eat finely baked thin bread or roasted sheep until he passed away. Anas added this description of the Prophet's food and dining habits.

Anas said, As far as I know, the Prophet never ate from a small individual dish, was never served finely baked thin bread, and never ate at a raised dining table. Qatadah was asked what they ate from. He replied, From cloths spread on the ground.

Anas said the Prophet married Safiyyah, and he invited the Muslims to the wedding feast. The Prophet ordered leather sheets to be spread out, then dates, dried yogurt, and butter were placed on them. Amr also reported from Anas that after the Prophet married her, he prepared a dish of dates, dried yogurt, and butter on a leather sheet.

Asma bint Abi Bakr said the people of Syria taunted her son Ibn al-Zubair, calling him the son of the woman with two waist-belts. She told him, My son, they taunt you about the two waist-belts. Do you know what they were? I split my waist-belt in two: with one half I tied the water-skin of the Messenger of Allah, and with the other I tied his food pouch. When the people of Syria taunted him, he answered with a line of poetry: Well then, that is a reproach whose shame is plainly yours, not mine.
